record_type_quote: This study includes two direct replications of Hosp, Hensley, Huddle, and Ford which found evidence of criterion-related validity of curriculum-based measurement (CBM) for reading and mathematics with postsecondary students with developmental disabilities (DD).

targets.authors: Hosp, J. L., Hensley, K., Huddle, S. M., & Ford, J. W.
targets.title: Using curriculum-based measures with postsecondary students with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
targets.evidence_quote: This study includes two direct replications of Hosp, Hensley, Huddle, and Ford which found evidence of criterion-related validity of curriculum-based measurement (CBM) for reading and mathematics with postsecondary students with developmental disabilities (DD).
targets.outcome_quote: This study, through two direct replications of a study on criterion-related validity, offers a model for replication assessment research and highlights the need through both replicated and nonreplicated findings.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The conclusion explicitly describes both replicated and nonreplicated findings: validity relations and the reading comparison replicated; math comparisons did not.

reasoning: Two independent cohorts directly re-test one published paper. No other specific original is re-tested; broader CBM literature is contextual.
